scope: Recorded outputs outside script decipherment; no analyses rerun
ranking_criteria: plausible novelty after bounded precedent search
readiness of source witnesses and reproducible aggregate outputs
usefulness to the candidate field and availability of a small publishable form
amount of external validation or rights work still required
search_boundary: Targeted live web searches and selected source openings; not an exhaustive literature review. Each record states whether its precedent judgment was checked or remains unchecked.

candidates.title: Exact solution set for the published 10/8/6 numerical proposal
candidates.field: Archaeological metrology; epigraphy and history of scholarship
candidates.audience: Researchers evaluating numerical readings and the original proposal
candidates.established: Under the two assumed equalities, four positive-integer triples solve the system: (4,20,36), (6,8,10), (10,8,6), and (36,20,4). The stated range restriction selects (10,8,6); the printed parity step does not establish that the short-stroke multiplier is even.

novelty.judgment: The exact conditional enumeration and correction are supported by the saved arithmetic; direct public literature precedents for this particular premise were not located in this package's bounded search. The proposal and archaeological joins remain prior claims.

candidates.missing_validation: Resolve the source object's identity and independently support the physical count/range before evaluating the equalities archaeologically; invite the proposal's author to review the correction.
candidates.smallest_form: Short commentary or correction letter
venues: Journal of Archaeological Science: Reports (short methods/commentary fit to confirm with editors)
an author correspondence with the original proposal's venue
candidates.remaining_work: Several days for source-by-source checking, author review, and a concise submission draft.

candidates.title: Susa marked weights: census and original-to-modern catalogue conflicts
candidates.field: Near Eastern archaeology; metrology; museum documentation
candidates.audience: Susa and Mesopotamian weight specialists, catalogue editors, museum registrars
candidates.established: The 2022 catalogue census contains 69 explicitly coded Susa entries and 57 usable mass/mark ratios. The later catalogue and Soutzo 1911 disagree on named duck weights: AS 13820 is 2769 g in the 1911 source and 3067 g in the 2022 catalogue; two originals describe ducks as unmarked while the newer catalogue records strokes. The source audit also separates manufacture from later deposition for SB 17774.

novelty.judgment: Source-to-source discrepancy tables may be useful to metrology and collection work; the close precedent search found archaeological catalogue data correction and data-paper models, not an equivalent Susa mark/mass census. Distinctive contribution remains provisional until accession conflicts are resolved.

candidates.missing_validation: Obtain full-resolution museum images, resolve two accession collisions, confirm dates and condition, and ask a Susa catalogue specialist to adjudicate original-to-modern object identity.
candidates.smallest_form: Source data note with a catalogue-maintainer correction table
venues: Journal of Open Archaeology Data (if rights-cleared dataset deposited)
candidates.remaining_work: One to two weeks plus external catalogue review; a public data-paper path also requires rights review.

candidates.title: Cross-source catalogue totals and component mismatches
candidates.field: Digital archaeology; catalogue scholarship; research data quality
candidates.audience: Curators, catalogue maintainers, archaeologists reusing structured catalogues
candidates.established: Independent table transcription finds 133 Lothal impressions versus 130 in prose and 62 single-impression objects versus 63. Tamil Nadu compound 4.19C differs between printed concordance and web array (six versus five components); the paper also reports four literal cross-route identifier differences. Gonur's account reports 26 tokens while each original figure panel depicts 23 representations. These counts describe distinct source assertions, not a resolved object total.
evidence_fields: Gonur Fig. 41 photo and drawing panel counts

novelty.judgment: The bounded search found an archaeological example of correcting catalogue-derived data and established data-paper outlets. It did not find these exact disagreements previously reported. Each discrepancy needs a maintainer response or primary ledger before correction claims are final.

candidates.missing_validation: Request the source registers and ask catalogue maintainers to confirm whether the differences are errors, scope differences, or transcription variants.
candidates.smallest_form: Short source-audit note or correction correspondence, split by catalogue owner if needed
venues: Journal of Open Archaeology Data (for a rights-cleared joined discrepancy dataset)
candidates.remaining_work: Several days to prepare an evidence table; external responses may take weeks.

candidates.title: Context and measurement completeness in the inscribed-object export
candidates.field: Archaeological data quality; digital heritage; corpus construction
candidates.audience: Indus archaeologists, corpus builders, metadata and provenance researchers
candidates.established: Across 5,680 rows and 4,695 numeric families, catalogue availability varies sharply by field. Only 1,444 rows from 1,163 families jointly contain area, room/grid, excavation label, depth and a chronological label. Of 69 objects in three source-defined Harappa cohorts, 60 join the export, but only two enter the complete RTL single-line length-at-least-three benchmark. The audit corrected missingness rules that had treated 2,870 depth placeholders and zero dimensions as observed values.
evidence_fields: source cohort join and filter counts

novelty.judgment: A useful description of selection and missingness in this particular export. BIAD Standards provide a close general precedent for archaeological data completeness and harmonization; a specific Indus export audit was not found in the bounded search.

candidates.missing_validation: Expert review of field semantics, improved object identifiers and a second corpus version comparison; release requires source and licensing review.
candidates.smallest_form: Data quality note with a reusable missingness and cohort table
venues: Journal of Open Archaeology Data if a reusable licensed dataset is deposited
candidates.remaining_work: One to two weeks for data dictionary, release review and independent reproduction.

candidates.title: Uncertainty-preserving transcription index for the 1979 sign chart
candidates.field: Digital epigraphy; digital archaeology; historical sign catalogues
candidates.audience: Indus epigraphers, corpus editors, sign-chart users and digitization researchers
candidates.established: The atlas indexes 687 source-linked cells. Independent numeric-label work includes a complete 175-cell reference for PDF20 columns 5-9 and a 337-cell reference for PDF21; comparison logged 22 initial disagreements, and post-comparison crop review retained 13 lower-code ambiguities. A separate fresh 20-cell spotcheck agreed jointly on 16/20, rank on 19/20, and code on 17/20. Two PDF20 lower codes and one upper rank were corrected from larger original crops; duplicate labels were retained rather than forced unique. These procedures audit printed numeric labels, not glyph identity or semantic accuracy.

novelty.judgment: The search found existing Indus sign charts and digitization work, but did not establish that this uncertainty-preserving linked index is unique. The resource's value is strongest as a citable derivative dataset after rights and expert review.
novelty.precedent_search: Partly checked; no exhaustive chart search

candidates.missing_validation: Independent epigraphic adjudication of uncertain cells, additional fresh numeric checks, accessibility testing, and explicit redistribution permission for chart imagery and derived crops.
candidates.smallest_form: Digital resource note or teaching resource
venues: Journal of Open Archaeology Data after rights-cleared deposition
candidates.remaining_work: Two to four weeks for expert annotation, rights review and durable hosting.

candidates.title: Museum, dataset, and excavation-publication coverage of Indus records
candidates.field: Digital archaeology; museum documentation; research infrastructure
candidates.audience: Indus archaeologists, museum data teams, corpus builders, digital heritage researchers
candidates.established: A bounded public-source census recorded 35 museum/institution rows and 15 dataset/archive entries, plus 87 site-name rows and four site-specific excavation-report titles across four sites. The sources do not support a complete global object denominator, and zero of 30 planned museum-to-corpus pairs met the explicit accession/excavation/CISI join rule. The result is a coverage map and a list of retrieval targets, not a completeness fraction.
evidence_fields: site-name rows and local corpus counts
coverage summary status and as_of date

novelty.judgment: The outputs organize dispersed public sources and show why a global coverage fraction cannot currently be calculated. The search located existing integrated Indus corpora and archaeological data-publication standards; novelty of the particular coverage map remains unchecked.
novelty.precedent_search: Partly checked; close digital-collection audits not searched exhaustively

candidates.missing_validation: Widen institution coverage, establish stable source snapshots, inspect the unreviewed dataset payloads, and validate a representative accession-to-corpus join sample before proposing an integrated resource.
candidates.smallest_form: Research data landscape note with a public source register
candidates.remaining_work: Several weeks for stronger source sampling and rights review; full register construction is a larger project.

candidates.title: Registration and face-layout frame for 22 Harappa tablets
candidates.field: Harappan archaeology; archaeological documentation; epigraphy
candidates.audience: Harappa excavators, Indus corpus editors, production and object-use researchers
candidates.established: The frame restores excavation unit/item keys for all 22 copied tablets and records 66 displayed faces. Sixteen objects are assigned to a unit-8040 clump; the remaining six are nearby or scattered. Seven direct stroke counts are readable (five with three strokes and two with four); all three faces on specimens 8 and 16 show 3,4,3. These are descriptions of published drawings and captions.
evidence_fields: published engraver group and deposition context

novelty.judgment: The object and production observations were published previously; the contribution is a source-to-catalogue join and machine-readable descriptive frame. General precedent search supports archaeological data publication, not a priority claim for the observations.
novelty.precedent_search: Checked at field level; exact-frame novelty unchecked

candidates.missing_validation: Independent coding from original objects or calibrated photographs, access to missing CISI plates and review of registration/context joins.
candidates.smallest_form: Short archaeological source-data note
venues: Journal of Open Archaeology Data if image rights permit
candidates.remaining_work: One to three weeks depending on access to full plates and second-coder review.

candidates.title: Lothal sealing recurrence, source counts, and physical-view frame
candidates.field: Harappan archaeology; sealings; archaeological science
candidates.audience: Lothal specialists, seal-impression researchers, experimental archaeologists
candidates.established: The source table covers 93 objects and 133 impressions; 68 objects join the corpus, and 29 eligible objects carry nine complete strings. G01 occurs on 11 objects across seven listed physical categories. The authors' prose instead reports 130 impressions. Among four G02 upper-zone observations, visible-cut ranges are 2–4, 3–5, 3–5 and 2–3, whose intersection is three; whole-object totals are unavailable. L206 is the only resolved contact example and contradicts one angular board-edge prediction.

novelty.judgment: The bounded search confirms established experimental clay-impression studies and archaeological data papers, but did not locate this exact Lothal source frame. The physical-use interpretation remains preliminary.

candidates.missing_validation: Calibrated full-object images and an independent blind coding of contact geometry; reconcile prose/table discrepancies with original logs.
candidates.smallest_form: Source frame and image-observation data note
candidates.remaining_work: Several weeks for measured images, coding reliability and reconciliation.

candidates.title: Kanmer pendant source frame and handling experiment
candidates.field: Harappan archaeology; archaeological science; object conservation
candidates.audience: Kanmer excavation researchers, seal and sealing specialists, conservation and experimental archaeology teams
candidates.established: The source frame covers eight related objects, including four clay pendants. Numbered reverse photographs are available for all four; three of four have restored registrations, dimensions/mass, individual trench/layer entries, and caption joins to scanner figures. The original three measure 32.5?34.1 mm long, 34.5?35.4 mm wide, 15.7?16.6 mm thick, and 15.0?15.7 g. No hole/wear measurement or direct laboratory date is available. A handling experiment is proposed, not run.

novelty.judgment: This is a source-frame and experiment-design contribution. The specimen interpretations and proposed handling use are prior scholarship; no bounded search established a new Kanmer use claim.
novelty.precedent_search: Partly checked; exact handling-study literature unchecked

candidates.missing_validation: Inspect the 2009 excavation article, final-volume object plates and CD-ROM; resolve all four registrations; make calibrated 3D measurements and run blind suspension/handling trials with replicated controls.
candidates.smallest_form: Source-data note followed by a measured experimental-methods note
candidates.remaining_work: Several weeks and institutional source access; physical trials require lab time.

candidates.title: Stroke and compound counts in the pinned Tamil Nadu graffiti catalogue
candidates.field: South Indian archaeology; epigraphy; catalogue data quality
candidates.audience: Tamil Nadu archaeologists, graffiti and early writing specialists, catalogue maintainers
candidates.established: The pinned catalogue snapshot has 480 plain-stroke occurrences and 194 explicit stroke compounds; 142 compounds have one stroke block plus one other component. A print/web check found four literal route-key differences and a six-versus-five component mismatch for 4.19C, specimen SGI(PPT)-G-0137. Aggregate API margins do not identify joint specimen rows or vessel quantities.
evidence_fields: printed concordance versus web component array

novelty.judgment: The search confirms broad catalogue and graffiti scholarship but did not locate this pinned-snapshot occurrence census. A publication would describe catalogue structure, not prove a numerical function or historical link to Indus signs.

candidates.missing_validation: Join aggregate records to registered specimen images, verify printed components against primary plates, and document portal versioning and reuse rights.
candidates.smallest_form: Catalogue data note with a specimen-level correction appendix
candidates.remaining_work: Two to four weeks for specimen joins, version pinning and rights review.

candidates.title: Original-source recovery for Gonur tokens and the Altyn Depe impressed object
candidates.field: Central Asian archaeology; object documentation; source history
candidates.audience: Margiana and Bactria archaeologists, token and sealing researchers
candidates.established: The original Gonur report describes 26 clay tokens near the palace's north entrance, while the photo and drawing panels each show 23 representations. The recovered Altyn Depe plate shows one object in three views and captions it as a tentative seal imprint from Excavation 5, horizon 11, room 18. No individual token inventory or impression count is supplied.
evidence_fields: Kircho et al. 2008 Plate 94.2 object views and caption

novelty.judgment: The contribution is recovering and separating original source claims and illustration counts; the underlying archaeology is prior. Search did not find a prior published reconciliation of the 26/23 discrepancy, but its cause is unknown.

candidates.missing_validation: Field inventory, individual token identities, original object photography, and archaeological review of the tentative impression classification.
candidates.smallest_form: Source note or illustrated catalogue correction request
venues: Iran (journal of the British Institute of Persian Studies)
candidates.remaining_work: Several days for a note; token-level dataset work depends on archive access.

candidates.title: Mass-to-mark variation in Susa weights and a Greater Indus catalogue audit
candidates.field: Metrology; Near Eastern archaeology; archaeological data science
candidates.audience: Weight and exchange-system specialists, Dholavira researchers
candidates.established: In a bounded Susa catalogue census, six displayed groups range from 1.921% to 99.773% minimum symmetric variation in mass per mark, with strong differences by shape/material/graphic family. The Greater Indus audit covered all 938 records, including 870 Dholavira objects, and found no explicit mark-related description terms; selected compressed Dholavira plates did not show a readable glyph joined to a mass.
evidence_fields: search terms and selected plate review

novelty.judgment: The exact bounded census appears useful; direct precedent search for this groupwise mass-per-mark variation analysis remains unchecked. Related metrology sources and prior source catalogue work exist.

candidates.missing_validation: Dated assemblages, high-resolution mark images, independent catalogue coding, and physical/museum confirmation of masses and condition.
candidates.smallest_form: Metrology data note with explicit null and date limits
candidates.remaining_work: Weeks to obtain specialist review and context/date fields.

candidates.title: Forward simulation of a flat stamp contacting curved clay
candidates.field: Experimental archaeology; contact mechanics; archaeological science
candidates.audience: Seal-impression analysts and experimental archaeologists
candidates.established: The recorded simulation predicts which parts of a flat engraved face contact a curved substrate under declared geometry and pressure assumptions. It supplies a prospective laboratory design; no physical experiment has yet tested the predictions. The related Lothal image study resolves only one contact example.

novelty.judgment: Live search found established curved-stamp contact and clay-impression experimental studies, so the general principle is not new. Whether this specific forward model adds a useful archaeological measurement protocol remains untested.

candidates.missing_validation: Run the proposed trials with measured stamp curvature, substrate geometry, pressure and replicate impressions; compare predicted and observed footprints blind.
candidates.smallest_form: Experimental methods note after physical validation; currently a teaching simulation
candidates.remaining_work: Two to six weeks depending on lab access and trial count.

candidates.title: Replication and grouping controls for a published khipu account match
candidates.field: Andean archaeology; computational archaeology; numerical record systems
candidates.audience: Khipu researchers, archaeologists of accounting, computational humanities researchers
candidates.established: The preserved coordinate alignment between UR068 and UR067 matches 16 of 20 published quantity columns, with total absolute error 16. The 60 lower values total 3,498 versus 3,482 in the upper reference row. Across 10,000 within-row shuffles, mean exact columns were 0.3213/20; the published alignment was the unique minimum-error case among 400 fixed relative shifts. This is a replication of a published alignment, not a complete numerical decoding.

novelty.judgment: Khipu computational work is an active area; the bounded search located a 2026 structural-pattern preprint but did not check the specific published UR068/UR067 source history. Exact replication priority is unchecked.

candidates.missing_validation: Khipu specialist confirmation of knot/cord coordinates and source transcription, along with a clear comparison to the original account's stated reconstruction procedure.
candidates.smallest_form: Replication note or teaching example in computational archaeology
candidates.remaining_work: One to three weeks for source-coordinate audit and specialist review.

candidates.title: Complete pooled inventories as constraints on noisy local membership
candidates.field: Computational archaeology; accounting history; conservation and error control
candidates.audience: Researchers modeling distributed records, noisy inventories and archaeological accounting systems
candidates.established: In 200 generated four-swap worlds, a 50% local support gate recovered 133 correct, 9 wrong and 58 ambiguous decoders. Adding a separately observed complete-pool conservation equation yielded 190 correct, 1 wrong and 9 ambiguous. The one remaining wrong answer passed the pooled equation but failed three independent count checks. This is a synthetic method demonstration.

novelty.judgment: General conservation constraints are well established; a direct search for this exact validation-selection comparison was not completed. Potential contribution is the controlled stress test, not the conservation idea itself.

candidates.missing_validation: Test on a source-defined real khipu or other inventory corpus with independent conservation totals and documented local membership error.
candidates.smallest_form: Methods note or classroom benchmark
candidates.remaining_work: Several weeks for source application and external methods review.

candidates.title: Calibration under copied records and shared recording quality
candidates.field: Statistical methods; computational humanities; dependence-aware inference
candidates.audience: Researchers using permutation references on copied or imperfectly transcribed records
candidates.established: In literal-copy simulations at nominal 5%, the record-wise reference rejected 15.9% while matched object references rejected 5.4%. For two imperfect faces, rejection was 11% versus 5%. In a separate shared-quality diagnostic, broad vector references rejected 94.2% and quality-conditioned references 1.0% for adjacent agreement; exact tails were 95.0% and 0.8%. The original nested predictor statistic was less sensitive (4% versus 3%).

novelty.judgment: Blockwise permutation methods preserving exchangeability are established (Zhou et al. 2014). The project result is a scenario-specific calibration stress test across copied records and shared recording quality; its broader contribution remains unchecked beyond this bounded search.

candidates.missing_validation: Reimplement independently outside the project, compare to established cluster permutation procedures and define which realistic acquisition mechanisms the synthetic cases represent.
candidates.smallest_form: Focused statistical methods note with executable examples
venues: Journal of Statistical Software if a general-purpose software contribution is isolated
Journal of Computational and Graphical Statistics
candidates.remaining_work: Two to four weeks for external implementation, literature comparison and a compact software package.

candidates.title: Exact finite sampling laws for uniqueness, deduplication, and unequal copies
candidates.field: Mathematical statistics; resampling methods; computational linguistics
candidates.audience: Researchers designing reference distributions after uniqueness filtering or duplicate collapse
candidates.established: The project enumerates a uniform 2,880-table subset induced by direct uniqueness conditioning from an 8,000-table binary space and demonstrates that deduplicating seven raw draws into six retained strings yields nonuniform support weights. A continuation-count sampler preserves latent and expanded margins for unequal multiplicities.

novelty.judgment: Exact sampling and conditional randomization have substantial prior literature. The small examples may teach consequences of filtering; the search did not establish a novel general theorem.

candidates.missing_validation: Place results against established exact conditional inference literature and obtain independent proof/code review; avoid a novelty claim unless a theorem or new algorithm is isolated.
candidates.smallest_form: Teaching example or methods appendix
venues: Journal of Statistical Software if a reusable package is developed
teaching example in Digital Scholarship in the Humanities
candidates.remaining_work: One to two weeks for proof-focused packaging and external methods review.

candidates.title: What counts distinguish ratios, scale, and wrong local assignments
candidates.field: Metrology; inverse problems; mathematical archaeology
candidates.audience: Researchers planning physical measurements for numerical systems
candidates.established: The saved generated-world studies separate relative-value recovery from absolute scale. In 200 four-swap worlds, a complete pooled inventory raises correct recovery from 133 to 190 and reduces wrong accepted values from 9 to 1 at the declared 50% gate. A validation design shows that with a counted unit anchor, one withheld count rejects all nine wrong local rays; without scale, count-first requires two checks. Vessel capacities alone retain rescaled unit/count alternatives.

novelty.judgment: The October 6 assessment found informal ratio-versus-scale precedents in proto-Elamite metrology and computational numeral disambiguation, but no direct formal identification-and-observation-ranking paper in its search. This remains an open, bounded novelty judgment, not a confirmed priority claim.
novelty.precedent_search: Checked in contribution assessment; needs independent expansion

candidates.missing_validation: Apply the acquisition design to a real source-defined collection with independently measured counts, known completeness and realistic measurement error.
candidates.smallest_form: Methods note on observation design, with generated worlds labeled as simulations
candidates.remaining_work: Several weeks for stronger precedents, independent software review and a real-data case.

candidates.title: Why the frozen chart-to-image OCR pipeline missed printed rows
candidates.field: Digital epigraphy; computer vision; archaeological data acquisition
candidates.audience: Digital epigraphers and teams building image-to-corpus pipelines
candidates.established: The frozen fresh20 endpoint matched row counts on 14/20 rows and recovered two whole-compatible rows at top one. Image review found top clipping in 18 target crops and following-row contamination in 14. A post-reference development geometry change raised matching row counts to 18/20, with six whole-compatible rows at top one and 16 at top five; this is not fresh validation. The chart reference used by the development pilot is an AI visual comparison to the historical chart and remains qualitative rather than expert gold.

novelty.judgment: OCR and chart digitization have extensive prior work; a failure diagnosis can still be a useful negative technical report. The bounded search did not establish novelty of the specific failure modes.

candidates.missing_validation: Freeze corrected crop rules and matcher before testing fresh source rows; have an independent image analyst assess crop boundaries.
candidates.smallest_form: Negative methods note or reproducibility case study
venues: Journal of Open Archaeology Data as a workflow/data resource
candidates.remaining_work: Two to four weeks for a new blind set and public-safe source permissions.

candidates.title: Source manifests, hash verification, and historical report checks
candidates.field: Research software; digital preservation; computational archaeology
candidates.audience: Small research teams preserving local-only source evidence and reproducible outputs
candidates.established: The historical report package records 1,568 selected evidence hashes verified, 23 root checks and eight methods checks. Several later source branches add independent verifiers that check source hashes, crop bounds, row accounting, IDs and output links. These are project-specific preservation tools, not a generalized archival platform.

novelty.judgment: Hash manifests and research-data verification are established practices. The package may serve as an applied case study; no claim to a new provenance method is supported.
novelty.precedent_search: Checked generally; exact tool comparison unchecked

candidates.missing_validation: Package one command-line tool with documentation, test fixtures, clean-environment replay and interoperability comparison to existing preservation tools.
candidates.smallest_form: Software note or internal reproducibility guide
candidates.remaining_work: Two to three weeks for package boundaries, docs and a clean-install review.

candidates.title: Documented failed routes for archaeological source acquisition
candidates.field: Digital archaeology; research infrastructure; source provenance
candidates.audience: Researchers repeating access work for hard-to-find excavation records and plates
candidates.established: Branch logs preserve failed retrievals and their remedies, including an initial 404 resolved by correcting a nested path, a PDF extraction failure that led to image-based inspection, unavailable institutional downloads, and source requests that remain unmade. The evidence is distributed across source-specific acquisition logs rather than normalized as one dataset.

novelty.judgment: Acquisition logs are standard research documentation. Their value is local reuse; the project has not normalized counts or searched for a comparable access-failure dataset.

candidates.missing_validation: Normalize route outcomes across packages, check URLs again, separate temporary outages from durable barriers, and ask source institutions before publication of access commentary.
candidates.smallest_form: Teaching example or appendix to a source-recovery note
candidates.remaining_work: Several days for a structured register; low standalone publication priority.

candidates.title: Reference-model selection and identifiability in generated administrative records
candidates.field: Computational archaeology; record linkage; latent-variable methods
candidates.audience: Researchers mapping symbols to known record systems and testing model selection
candidates.established: In generated systems, a fresh reference-only selector recovers 309/384 maps, compared with 283 for a fixed graph profile and 168 for slot-only mapping. Exact certificates distinguish search misses from an objective preferring a wrong map. A separate rational-rank calculation identifies fixed three-component product profiles up to label permutation; collapsed components remain nonidentifiable.

novelty.judgment: Known-reference mapping and latent mixture identification have close precedents, including decipherment and administrative-record studies. The generated comparison is useful for methods training; the assessment found no support for a broad novelty claim.
novelty.precedent_search: Checked in contribution assessment; exact venue review remains

candidates.missing_validation: Demonstrate on a real record system with independently known mappings and an acquisition process not generated by the model; compare against current mapping software.
candidates.smallest_form: Teaching benchmark or software appendix
venues: Transactions of the Association for Computational Linguistics (unlikely without a broader NLP contribution)
candidates.remaining_work: Weeks for a real-data validation; current synthetic case is supplementary material at most.

candidates.title: Grouped prediction and restoration controls for short Indus records
candidates.field: Computational epigraphy; computational linguistics; statistical archaeology
candidates.audience: Researchers comparing predictive structure in short, duplicated archaeological records
candidates.established: The preserved unique-text evaluation reports a 0.84836-bit gain per noninitial sign under the alias-preserving split. The one-known-slot restoration evaluation reaches 33.81% exact top-one on 8,009 masks, and the matched unknown-gap estimator scores 46.30% against 51.07% for always predicting one. The gain is a measure of predictive structure and does not identify a language or meaning.

novelty.judgment: The October 6 live precedent assessment found Yadav et al. 2010's deduplicated held-out restoration, plus other Indus restoration and non-specificity results. Object/alias grouping and the joint accuracy/loss tradeoff are narrower candidate contributions; publication priority is plausible but not a general first restoration claim.
novelty.precedent_search: Checked in the October 6 assessment; a broader search is needed before submission

candidates.missing_validation: Independent reproduction, reviewed source transcription, comparison to a faithful published baseline, and a genuinely fresh expert-annotated evaluation block.
candidates.smallest_form: Workshop paper or methods note; retain the failed gap-count result as a negative comparison
candidates.remaining_work: One to two weeks for related-work correction and a reviewer-ready reproduction package; fresh annotation would take longer.

registry_coverage.statement: Every registered ID is assigned to one inventory candidate. Related statistical endpoints are consolidated when they test the same publication contribution. A separate, unregistered October 6 evidence-census package is included as a timely data-landscape candidate.
